authors: Javad Bakhshi, Petr Matous, Lynn Crawford
method: systematic review of 636 articles; bibliographic coupling
geography_sector: project governance (global corpus; megaprojects, PPPs, networks)
definition: PMI (2021): PG = 'guidance of project activities through frameworks, processes, and functions aligned with strategic, organizational, and operational objectives.' Müller (2016): controls / processes / relationships.
stakeholders: Principals/agents, stakeholders, networks across levels; conflict theorised per lens.
temporality_detail: Flags temporal governance as a gap. 'opportunities to explore temporal governance... how time-sensitive adaptations (e.g., to market or regulatory changes) impact project viability' (p. 11); 'sociopolitical changes as critical triggers for governance adaptations... often inadequately addressed.'
misalignment_detail: Field-level confirmation that temporal & sociopolitical-trigger governance is under-theorised - precisely the thesis's space.
gaps: Names the missing agenda (temporal governance; sociopolitical triggers) without filling it.
key_quotes: 'opportunities to explore temporal governance... how time-sensitive adaptations (e.g., to market or regulatory changes) impact project viability' (p. 11).
coding_notes: Most authoritative recent field map; legitimizes the thesis gap statement.
